record.original_question: Does an analogue of Dunwoody’s theorem hold for totally disconnected locally compact groups, that is, must a tdlc group of rational discrete cohomological dimension at most 1 be topologically isomorphic to the fundamental group of a graph of profinite groups?

evidence.quote: Does an analogue of Dunwoody’s theorem hold for totally disconnected locally compact groups, that is, must a tdlc group of rational discrete cohomological dimension at most 1 be topologically isomorphic to the fundamental group of a graph of profinite groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact (tdlc) Hausdorff topological group. Recall that for such a group one defines the rational discrete cohomological dimension $\mathrm{cd}_{\mathbb{Q}}(G)$ as the cohomological dimension of $G$ in the abelian category of rational discrete $G$-modules (i.e. $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces $V$ with a $G$-action such that the stabilizer of every $v\in V$ is open in $G$). A graph of profinite groups is a graph of groups (in the sense of Bass–Serre theory) whose vertex and edge groups are profinite groups, with edge maps being continuous injective homomorphisms; its fundamental group carries a natural tdlc topology in which the vertex (and edge) groups embed as compact open subgroups.

Dunwoody's theorem states that a discrete group has cohomological dimension at most $1$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ if and only if it is the fundamental group of a graph of finite groups whose vertex group orders are invertible in $\mathbb{Q}$ (equivalently, finite).

Question: If $G$ is a tdlc group with $\mathrm{cd}_{\mathbb{Q}}(G) \le 1$, must $G$ be topologically isomorphic to the fundamental group of a graph of profinite groups?
artifact.status_search_result: The analogue of Dunwoody's theorem has been established under additional hypotheses: a compactly generated, unimodular, CO-bounded tdlc group $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{cd}_{\mathbb{Q}}(G)\le 1$ if and only if $G$ is the fundamental group of a finite graph of profinite groups (Castellano–Corob Cook–Marchionna, arXiv:2201.10847). The authors explicitly state they could not prove the result in full generality and pose related questions, so the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Unimodular totally disconnected locally compact groups of rational discrete cohomological dimension one
status_evidence.snippet: A compactly generated CO-bounded t.d.l.c. group G of rational discrete cohomological dimension at most 1 is isomorphic to the fundamental group of a finite graph of profinite groups.
status_evidence.claim: The analogue of Dunwoody's theorem holds under compact generation, unimodularity and CO-boundedness, but the authors note they could not prove it in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Subgroups, hyperbolicity and cohomological dimension for totally disconnected locally compact groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies cohomological dimension for tdlc groups and related finiteness conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on rational discrete cohomological dimension for tdlc groups, indicating the general Dunwoody analogue is treated as an open question.
